A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeuCLIP work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across table renumbering and the relocation of the LLM-use disclosure.

before.justification: V1 reports original CLIP training experiments on five datasets, zero-shot classification and retrieval results, ablations, normalizer-error measurements, and runtime profiling.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds compute-adjusted comparisons, memory measurements, sensitivity analyses, and revised DFN-1B results.

M1.justification: The unified objective, prototype-based NPN architecture, alternating updates, multiple NPN steps, and periodic restarts remain unchanged in Equations (10)–(12) and Algorithm 1. The new Algorithm 4 is explicitly a simplified surrogate for theoretical analysis.

E1.justification: Both versions train on CC3M, CC12M, DFN-14M, DFN-192M, and DFN-1B and evaluate the same 38 Datacomp tasks. Added experiments vary compute, batch size, and NPN settings within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: The original comparisons retain OpenCLIP, FastCLIP, SigLIP, and AmorLIP. V2 adds a compute-adjusted comparison against the first three methods while explicitly omitting AmorLIP (Table 13), and a memory comparison against OpenCLIP alone (Table 6).

E3.justification: The reported DFN-1B training budget increases from 1 billion to 3 billion processed samples, with the encoder and batch size retained (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 1). V2 also introduces compute matching by shortening NeuCLIP training according to NPN overhead, assuming equal baseline iteration costs. Additional protocols vary prototype count and test DFN-14M normalizer error at batch sizes 512 and 4,096.

E4.justification: V2 adds prototype-count sensitivity on DFN-14M and CC12M, restart-frequency sensitivity on CC12M, and a DFN-14M batch-size normalizer-error analysis (Tables 19–21 and Figures 4b and 5). New memory profiling and compute-adjusted comparisons also examine whether NPN overhead undermines the efficiency advantage, extending v1's runtime analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report three runs with different random seeds and means with standard deviations for CC3M, CC12M, and DFN-14M. No changed repetition counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are reported. The new memory table uses the existing plus/minus reporting style.

E6.justification: Under the increased DFN-1B budget, NeuCLIP's Datacomp Average changes from 53.74 to 57.34 and FastCLIP's from 53.57 to 56.68; these are results under different training budgets. The other four main dataset comparisons are unchanged. V2 adds compute-adjusted, memory, and sensitivity results, removes the DFN-14M restart-12,500 result, and corrects the reproduced FastCLIP row from 25.08/31.89 to 24.74/31.50 for CC3M/CC12M (v1 Table 11; v2 Table 12).

T1.justification: V2 adds Appendix C with Algorithm 4, explicit assumptions, six lemmas, Theorem 2, proofs, and a claimed O(epsilon^-4) stochastic-gradient complexity bound. V1 contains the loss reformulation and cited convergence arguments but no corresponding analysis. The added Lemma 2 has an incorrect bound as stated: f(x,y)=0.05y^2-xy+5.5x^2 satisfies its assumptions with mu=L22=0.1, L11=11, and L12=L21=1, yet y*(x)=10x has sensitivity 10, exceeding the claimed bound of 2.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: reformulating contrastive loss, learning compact neural normalizers with a unified objective, alternating optimization, and empirical advantages over existing methods.

C2.justification: V2 removes the explanation that DFN-1B performs worse because of its smaller training budget. It adds interpretations concerning negligible memory overhead and performance after compute adjustment, together with the baseline-cost assumptions and AmorLIP omission. Appendix C explicitly limits its analysis to a modified algorithm under assumptions.

D1.justification: V2 adds a NeuCLIP code-access link, specifies hyperparameter selection by Datacomp Average, explains linear warmup, and documents NPN search ranges. It also explains full-dataset embedding computation and 10,000 sampled queries for measuring normalizer error. These largely clarify previously undocumented procedures. The timing table replaces dataset labels with embedding dimensions.

R1.justification: V2 adds embedding-geometry work by Chou and Alam and by Pal et al., plus references supporting the new convergence analysis, including Guo, Lin, Liu, Nouiehed, and Yuan. The central positioning relative to FastCLIP, AmorLIP, and TempNet remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The existing narrative and section order are largely retained. Changes include localized explanations, correcting 'SigCLIP' to 'SigLIP,' updating the publication header and affiliation, adding acknowledgments, and inserting the convergence appendix before the relocated LLM-use disclosure.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the experimental displays with memory and compute-adjusted comparison tables, prototype and restart ablation tables, Figure 5, and an additional Figure 4 panel. It moves the settings table into the main text, changes timing-table columns, and changes Figure 4's dataset-size comparison axis from samples seen in millions to percentage. The original main figures otherwise retain their design.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support and reproducibility through compute-adjusted comparisons, memory measurements, additional sensitivity checks, corrected FastCLIP values, and code and measurement details. These address limitations of v1's equal-sample comparisons and documentation. The net gain is limited: compute matching assumes baseline costs and omits AmorLIP, while the added convergence proof concerns a modified algorithm and relies on the incorrect Lemma 2 bound.
